previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, multiple pulmonary emboli, and recent pneumonia was admitted after a fall with elevated creatine kinase, indicating rhabdomyolysis. She developed acute kidney injury, hyponatremia, and weakness. Workup revealed a new pulmonary embolism, urinary tract infection, and persistent pneumonia. She was treated with IV fluids, antibiotics, anticoagulation, and supportive care. A muscle biopsy was performed to evaluate for toxic myopathy. Her condition improved over 18 days, with resolution of infection, stabilization of kidney function, and gradual strength recovery. She was discharged home on supplemental oxygen with plans for follow-up and outpatient management of her muscle disorder.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Other dependence on machines, supplemental oxygen

Mrs. ___ is a  ___ year old morbidly obese woman with a

# SOB: Mrs. ___ has known LVH with normal LVEF. She had a 
recent admission ___ for polymyositis flare which was 
treated with high dose steroids and was discharged on slow 
taper. She was now was admitted for progressive SOB on exertion 
from 400 to a few feet, accompanied, in the week prior to 
admission, by bil ankle swelling and weight gain of 19 lbs 
despite an increase in her Lasix from 20mg to 40mg daily and 
decrease in her steroids from Methylprednisolone 32mg to 28mg 
daily prior to admission. She also had her second infusion of 
Rituximab on the day prior to presentation. On admission to the 
ED she was hemodynamically stable and well saturated on room air 
at rest. She underwent CTA which ruled out recurrence of PE and 
demonstrated interstitial pulmonary edema. She was concluded to 
have diastolic CHF exacerbation due to fluid retention secondary 
to high dose steroids. Rituximab is also known to cause edema 
and may have contributed to this process. On the floor she was 
given one dose of IV furosemide 40mg and had excellent urinary 
response with I/O of negative 5 liter in 24h. She subsequently 
reported significant symptomatic improvement. She was discharged 
on oral furosemide 40mg BID. Her weight on discharge was 408.5. 
She will require careful daily monitoring of her weight, strict 
adherence to a low sodium diet and optimal blood pressure 
control in the out-patient setting. Follow-up with her PCP was 
arranged.   
.

symptoms have since gradually improved and CK, troponin, LFTs 
are all trending down. She was continued on Azathioprine and 
Methylprednisolone at 28mg and is planned for continued slow 
taper of her steroid dose by 4mg every ___. She will continue 
Bactrim prophylaxis and Rituximab therapy as per her 
rheumatologist.

Discharge Instructions:
You came in because of SOB, likely secondary to fluid retention 
secondary to the steroid medication you were taking. You had a 
CT of your chest which ruled out a clot in your lungs. You were 
however found to be fluid overloaded and were treated with 
diuretic medication with a large urinary response. As discussed 
prior to your discharge control of the amount of salt in your 
diet, careful monitoring of your weight and good control of your 
hypertension as well as adherence to your medication regimen are 
all key in preventing further worsening and recurrence of fluid 
overload.
